To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the emission wavelength of AlGaN MQW LEDs decreases and the fraction TE polarized light emission of the light emission increases with the Al content in the AlGaN barrier.
the Al mole fraction in AlGaN barriers around the quantum well has a large impact on the external efficiency of AlGaN MQW LEDs emitting around 260–280 nm.
for a fixed current density, the on-waiver emission power reaches a local maximum when the Al mole fraction in an Al x Ga1-x N barrier around a Al0.53 Ga0.47 N quantum well is x = 67%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the barrier composition on electro optical properties of UVC light emitters.
the impact of the barrier Al mole fraction on the electro-optical performance of AlGaN MQW LEDs.
the influence of the barrier composition on the emission wavelength, optical emission profile, and light output of AlGaN quantum-well light emitters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Al x Ga 1−x N composition of the AlGaN MQW barrier has a significant influence on the electro-optical properties, such as emission wavelength and polarization as well as emission power, of AlGaN UV LEDs emitting around 260 nm.

the barrier height of Al x Ga1-x N barriers has a significant influence on the electro-optical properties in AlGaN-based LEDs emitting in the UVC regime, and that the emission wavelength and the optical polarization are strongly affected by the Al mole fraction in Al x Ga1 − x N barriers.
for Al x Ga1-x N MQW UVC-LEDs, the barrier Al composition should be chosen such that the emission power at a certain current density is maximized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the emission wavelength and optical polarization of UVC light emitters can be tuned by the Al content in the barrier, whereas the emission power is mainly limited by the charge carrier injection efficiency and electrical confinement.
the Al mole fraction of the Al x Ga _{1-x} N barrier in AlGaN-based MQWs emitting around 270nm is a crucial parameter that determines the emission power and optical polarization of UVC LEDs.
the emission power of the UVC AlGaN MQW LEDs can be improved by increasing the Al mole fraction in Al x Ga1-x N barriers up to a certain limit, where the emission power starts to decrease again.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the barrier composition has a strong influence on the performance of AlGaN UVC light emitting devices and should be carefully chosen for a given device structure.
the emission power of AlGan UVC LEDs is strongly influenced by the height of the AlGaN barrier around the quantum well.
the emission power of AlGan-based UVC light-emitting diodes can be increased by optimizing the barrier composition.
